- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Revert #8446 (`2cfbc2ca2b8199f51444bace2bd796674be195c3`) to restore the previous CODEOWNERS approval process.

- Restore `noamelf/codeowner-multi-approval-action@v0.1` and require reinforcement-learning team approval for `tdene` again.
- Remove the repository-owned approval checker, its tests, and its CI invocation and dependency.
- Restore the prior review-label logic, including its API-error handling and final-review stage decision. This is a complete revert of #8446, including the subsequent blocker fix that was part of the merged PR.

Preserve the later workflow input cleanup from #8658.

## Issue tracking

Reverts #8446.

nodes.body:
Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository. Workflows must be run manually.

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/auto-sync).

🔄 Merge queue validation started!

You can track the progress here: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/41159118651

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

The revert restores the requested approval policy, but also reintroduces three review-label logic failures: failed team lookups can permit approval, final-review blockers can be ignored, and failed review retrieval can remove valid approval labels.

### Abort label updates when active reviews cannot be retrieved

**Failure:** Consider a non-draft PR changing `megatron/training/training.py`, with a training approval and an existing `Approved` label. If the GraphQL request fails, [_get_latest_reviews](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L162-L180) now returns `{}`. The caller interprets that as a successful empty review history, marks training pending, and [removes `Approved`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L248-L275). A PR in Final Review can similarly be demoted to expert review. The workflow then succeeds despite having changed labels using unavailable data. Expected behavior is to abort without label mutations. Responses containing GraphQL errors alongside readable partial data are also no longer rejected.

**Correction:** Restore failure propagation and explicit GraphQL-error rejection in `_get_latest_reviews`. Keep the previous request timeout so an unavailable API cannot leave evaluation waiting indefinitely. Suggested patch, targeting that function:

```diff
                 headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"},
+                timeout=30,
             )
             resp.raise_for_status()
-            nodes = resp.json()["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["latestReviews"]["nodes"]
+            payload = resp.json()
+            if payload.get("errors"):
+                raise RuntimeError("GitHub returned errors while fetching latest reviews")
+            nodes = payload["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["latestReviews"]["nodes"]
             for node in nodes:
                 if node["author"]:
                     reviews[node["author"]["login"]] = node["state"]
         except Exception as e:
-            logger.warning(f"Could not get latest reviews for PR #{pr_number}: {e}")
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Could not get latest reviews for PR #{pr_number}") from e
```

The invariant is that unsuccessful or partial review retrieval never reaches label mutation; a successfully retrieved empty history must remain distinct from failure.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Use a training-only fixture with nonempty training membership. From Expert Review, Final Review, and Approved, simulate transport/HTTP failure, an error-only GraphQL response, errors accompanied by readable data, and malformed data after one parsed review: each must raise and call neither label-add nor label-remove. Assert `timeout=30`. Separately, successful empty `nodes` must still leave training pending and remove a stale `Approved` label; a valid training approval without blockers must still permit advancement. Preserve draft no-op behavior and dismissal handling through successful latest-review results. Retain the exception/no-mutation assertions from the [deleted API-error tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L242-L258), replacing their intentionally removed RL-exemption setup.

For these findings, keep label-only regressions independent of the deleted checker and invoke them from [linting CI](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/.github/workflows/cicd-main.yml#L651-L666). All suggested changes were traced statically through the callers and handlers, but must be verified before adoption. Tests were not executed; the external action's implementation is not available in the mounted trees.

> **Note:** formal approval is not available for this request, so this review is posted as a comment only.

*Review generated by codex. This was a full review. Request a full review with `/review reset=true`.*

<!-- nemo-ci-review-rendering:inline-v1 -->
<!-- nemo-ci-formal-review:f2d82f58374217e20006ef321aa83cc5e18797a54d6b278c8b6b3761fe4c9bfe:582106f780a4660b88b47e3bf255d2094d8385d1d0ba451e19b67f8621e8f2ae -->

### A failed team lookup can mark an unapproved PR Approved

**Failure:** For a non-draft training-only PR with no reviews, make `get_team_by_slug("training")` raise. This branch caches an empty set. Training is added to `pending_expert_teams`, but the [pending-reviewer calculation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L209-L233) expands that team to no users. Consequently, the [expert-stage handler](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L304-L324) adds `Approved` without any training approval. Required final-team lookup failures can likewise allow Final Review to advance. The nearby claim that this fallback is conservative is therefore incorrect.

**Correction:** Abort evaluation rather than cache unavailable membership as an empty successful result. Replace this line with:

```suggestion
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not get members for team {slug}") from e
```

Update the comment above the pending-team loops accordingly. This retains successful membership caching while restoring the invariant that failed membership retrieval cannot authorize label changes.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed:** With `megatron/training/training.py`, no reviews, and training lookup failing, assert an exception and no label additions/removals from each of Expert Review, Final Review, and Approved. Also cover an exception during membership pagination. For `megatron/core/config.py`, one core team approving while the other team's lookup fails must not advance or change labels. Successful lookups must retain these distinct cases: missing training approval stays pending; training approval without blockers permits advancement; a missing required core-team approval routes to Final Review; both required core-team approvals permit advancement. Successful repeated lookups must remain cached, and failures must not cache an empty membership. Preserve the exception/no-mutation assertions from the [deleted team-failure regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L267-L273), without depending on the removed author exemption. Suggested code is source-reasoned, not executed.

### Keep final-team change requests blocking expert-stage advancement

**Failure:** Take a non-draft PR changing only `megatron/training/training.py`, with no review-stage label. Let a training member approve and a `core-nemo` member request changes. Training is satisfied, `final_required` is empty, and `pending_final` contains the core reviewer. This assignment nevertheless makes `needs_final_review` false, so the [expert-stage handler](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L304-L324) adds `Approved` despite the outstanding change request. The same failure applies to a `core-adlr` reviewer. Expected behavior is to enter Final Review until that blocker is resolved, consistent with the other stage handlers.

**Correction:** Restore the blocker-aware decision without restoring the author exemption:

```suggestion
        needs_final_review = bool(final_required or final_non_approvers)
```

The invariant is that an active final-team change request blocks approval even when changed files do not require that team's CODEOWNERS approval.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed:** With training membership `{trainer}`, core memberships containing distinct reviewers, and reviews `{trainer: APPROVED, core-reviewer: CHANGES_REQUESTED}`, assert that Expert Review adds only `Final Review`, testing each core team. With no core blocker, the same approved training-only PR must add `Approved`; with training still pending, it must not advance. A required core-team approval must remain necessary for core-owned changes. Retain the [deleted blocker tests'](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L193-L229) distinctions: a core approval is not a blocker; an active core change request keeps Final Review pending; from Approved it removes `Approved` and restores Final Review. Adapt their setup to satisfy training approval rather than rely on the removed RL exemption. Drafts must remain unchanged. Suggested code and checks were traced statically, not executed.

### A failed team lookup can mark an unapproved PR Approved

**Failure:** For a non-draft training-only PR with no reviews, make `get_team_by_slug("training")` raise. This branch caches an empty set. Training is added to `pending_expert_teams`, but the [pending-reviewer calculation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L209-L233) expands that team to no users. Consequently, the [expert-stage handler](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L304-L324) adds `Approved` without any training approval. Required final-team lookup failures can likewise allow Final Review to advance. The nearby claim that this fallback is conservative is therefore incorrect.

**Correction:** Abort evaluation rather than cache unavailable membership as an empty successful result. Replace this line with:

```suggestion
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not get members for team {slug}") from e
```

Update the comment above the pending-team loops accordingly. This retains successful membership caching while restoring the invariant that failed membership retrieval cannot authorize label changes.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed:** With `megatron/training/training.py`, no reviews, and training lookup failing, assert an exception and no label additions/removals from each of Expert Review, Final Review, and Approved. Also cover an exception during membership pagination. For `megatron/core/config.py`, one core team approving while the other team's lookup fails must not advance or change labels. Successful lookups must retain these distinct cases: missing training approval stays pending; training approval without blockers permits advancement; a missing required core-team approval routes to Final Review; both required core-team approvals permit advancement. Successful repeated lookups must remain cached, and failures must not cache an empty membership. Preserve the exception/no-mutation assertions from the [deleted team-failure regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L267-L273), without depending on the removed author exemption. Suggested code is source-reasoned, not executed.

### Keep final-team change requests blocking expert-stage advancement

**Failure:** Take a non-draft PR changing only `megatron/training/training.py`, with no review-stage label. Let a training member approve and a `core-nemo` member request changes. Training is satisfied, `final_required` is empty, and `pending_final` contains the core reviewer. This assignment nevertheless makes `needs_final_review` false, so the [expert-stage handler](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L304-L324) adds `Approved` despite the outstanding change request. The same failure applies to a `core-adlr` reviewer. Expected behavior is to enter Final Review until that blocker is resolved, consistent with the other stage handlers.

**Correction:** Restore the blocker-aware decision without restoring the author exemption:

```suggestion
        needs_final_review = bool(final_required or final_non_approvers)
```

The invariant is that an active final-team change request blocks approval even when changed files do not require that team's CODEOWNERS approval.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed:** With training membership `{trainer}`, core memberships containing distinct reviewers, and reviews `{trainer: APPROVED, core-reviewer: CHANGES_REQUESTED}`, assert that Expert Review adds only `Final Review`, testing each core team. With no core blocker, the same approved training-only PR must add `Approved`; with training still pending, it must not advance. A required core-team approval must remain necessary for core-owned changes. Retain the [deleted blocker tests'](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L193-L229) distinctions: a core approval is not a blocker; an active core change request keeps Final Review pending; from Approved it removes `Approved` and restores Final Review. Adapt their setup to satisfy training approval rather than rely on the removed RL exemption. Drafts must remain unchanged. Suggested code and checks were traced statically, not executed.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

The revert restores the requested approval policy, but also reintroduces three review-label logic failures: failed team lookups can permit approval, final-review blockers can be ignored, and failed review retrieval can remove valid approval labels.

### Abort label updates when active reviews cannot be retrieved

**Failure:** Consider a non-draft PR changing `megatron/training/training.py`, with a training approval and an existing `Approved` label. If the GraphQL request fails, [_get_latest_reviews](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L162-L180) now returns `{}`. The caller interprets that as a successful empty review history, marks training pending, and [removes `Approved`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/swap_pr_labels.py#L248-L275). A PR in Final Review can similarly be demoted to expert review. The workflow then succeeds despite having changed labels using unavailable data. Expected behavior is to abort without label mutations. Responses containing GraphQL errors alongside readable partial data are also no longer rejected.

**Correction:** Restore failure propagation and explicit GraphQL-error rejection in `_get_latest_reviews`. Keep the previous request timeout so an unavailable API cannot leave evaluation waiting indefinitely. Suggested patch, targeting that function:

```diff
                 headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"},
+                timeout=30,
             )
             resp.raise_for_status()
-            nodes = resp.json()["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["latestReviews"]["nodes"]
+            payload = resp.json()
+            if payload.get("errors"):
+                raise RuntimeError("GitHub returned errors while fetching latest reviews")
+            nodes = payload["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["latestReviews"]["nodes"]
             for node in nodes:
                 if node["author"]:
                     reviews[node["author"]["login"]] = node["state"]
         except Exception as e:
-            logger.warning(f"Could not get latest reviews for PR #{pr_number}: {e}")
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Could not get latest reviews for PR #{pr_number}") from e
```

The invariant is that unsuccessful or partial review retrieval never reaches label mutation; a successfully retrieved empty history must remain distinct from failure.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Use a training-only fixture with nonempty training membership. From Expert Review, Final Review, and Approved, simulate transport/HTTP failure, an error-only GraphQL response, errors accompanied by readable data, and malformed data after one parsed review: each must raise and call neither label-add nor label-remove. Assert `timeout=30`. Separately, successful empty `nodes` must still leave training pending and remove a stale `Approved` label; a valid training approval without blockers must still permit advancement. Preserve draft no-op behavior and dismissal handling through successful latest-review results. Retain the exception/no-mutation assertions from the [deleted API-error tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7d6895ac6a3ee9e16c53f573f363d2a52b88bf94/tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_codeowners_approval.py#L242-L258), replacing their intentionally removed RL-exemption setup.

For these findings, keep label-only regressions independent of the deleted checker and invoke them from [linting CI](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cbc3ef0f4e0d7b286dd518d0f555da3e210b13c/.github/workflows/cicd-main.yml#L651-L666). All suggested changes were traced statically through the callers and handlers, but must be verified before adoption. Tests were not executed; the external action's implementation is not available in the mounted trees.
